text:
security-bot: :rotating_light: Suspicious access pattern detected. Service account 'svc-user-sync' performed cross-org read on 3 projects outside its assigned scope. AuditID=aq-7f3b2

maya: seeing the bot alert — I just pulled the audit logs. Looks like after yesterday's RBAC refactor a policy path got widened. snippet:

```
{"timestamp":"2025-10-04T15:12:03Z","actor":"svc-user-sync","action":"project.read","resource":"org:acme:project:billing","policy_match":"allow","policy_id":"rbac-refactor-v2"}
```

james: ugh. which change exactly? PR?

maya: PR 7843 merged 02:30 UTC yesterday. The change consolidated 'team_*' group rules and added a fallback allow for legacy-service-roles. I think that fallback is too permissive.

sam: recommend immediate mitigation: 1) revoke svc-user-sync tokens, 2) add a temporary deny rule for cross-org reads, 3) rollback the fallback allow if easy. Who can revoke tokens now? :lock:

james: I can revoke the service principal creds. Doing revoke now: `authctl revoke svc-user-sync --all`

deploy-bot: deploy-trigger: revocation job queued on auth-plane, job id dj-9921.

maya: thanks. I'm running a query for all actions that svc-user-sync did in last 24h. Quick results — 412 read actions, 18 of which were outside allowed projects. Listing top targets: billing, payroll, partner-integration.

irene: any indication of data exfil? Need to know if PII accessed. If so, we trigger customer-notify runbook and legal.

maya: preliminary: reads were metadata-level for billing reports (invoice ids, amounts). No obvious full PII blobs returned. Still investigating payloads — looking at request logs now.

james: rollback PR 7843? That will require a small migration revert. I can open revert PR and hotfix the policy engine. But we should put an emergency deny in place first so rollback isn't the only stopgap.

sam: agreed. I'll push a deny patch: `rbacctl patch --add-deny "svc-user-sync:project.read:!project:allowed"` and apply to policy-plane. Pushing in 30s.

maya: applying deny now to policy-plane (canary region us-west-2 first). Patch id: deny-2025-10-04-1. Monitoring logs for blocked requests.

security-bot: Canary applied in us-west-2. 24 blocked requests in last 2m.

maya: confirm that blocked requests dropped to zero after deny applied. Good. I'll continue full scan.

james: opened PR 7901 to revert fallback allow and add tests that assert explicit deny precedence. Link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/7901 :eyes:

irene: good. Start the customer-notify draft just in case. I'll hold on sending until we confirm PII unaffected. Add timeline and mitigation steps.

maya: one more oddity — KMS logs show svc-user-sync requested DECRYPT on a key tied to partner-integration. The request returned success before the RBAC change, but the policy allowed it via role binding. We should rotate the key and audit key policy bindings.

james: calling key rotation now for the partner-integration key. `kmsctl rotate --key partner-integration --force`

sam: note for ops — rotating keys will break integrations briefly. Notify SRE/owners.

deploy-bot: key-rotation job kr-447 scheduled. Expected propagation 45s.

maya: after rotation, decrypt requests from svc-user-sync failed. Good. So we cut active access.

security-bot: Incident severity set to P2. Ticket created: INC-2025-449.

irene: please log all affected customers in the incident ticket. I'll prepare the notification template.

maya: initial root cause hypothesis: RBAC refactor introduced a fallback allow rule for legacy-service-roles that accidentally matched svc-user-sync via group inheritance. Fix path: remove fallback, add explicit deny tests, add unit/regression tests to policy engine, and add an audit alert for any cross-org project.read by service accounts.

james: timeline: revoke tokens 15:16, deny patch 15:18 canary, key rotate 15:20, revert PR opened 15:25. PR to ship after review with canary rollout 15:40.

sam: postmortem owners? maya + james, cc irene. I'll attach logs and mitigation commands to the ticket.

maya: quick ask — can we add an automated pre-merge check that runs policy-sim against a sample of service accounts to catch fallback allow matches? That would've caught this.

james: agreed. I'll add policy-sim to CI for infra PRs.

irene: good. After action items: 1) customer notification if PII found, 2) update RBAC doc, 3) CI policy-sim, 4) longer-term: KMS access audit dashboard.

maya: updating the ticket with artifacts and the full log dump. Will follow up with a brief postmortem draft tomorrow. :pray:

sam: nice work everyone. Triage closed for now; will reopen if new findings surface. :white_check_mark:
